title: Elasticities of demand and supply
summary: Elasticity measures responsiveness. PED links price changes to total revenue, YED shows how demand changes as incomes grow, and PES shows how easily producers can respond.

keyterms.definition: Responsiveness of quantity demanded to a change in price: PED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔP.
When |PED| > 1: quantity demanded changes by a larger percentage than price.
When |PED| < 1: quantity demanded changes by a smaller percentage than price.
When |PED| = 1: the percentage change in quantity equals the percentage change in price, so total revenue is unchanged.
Number and closeness of substitutes, necessity versus luxury, share of income spent and time period.
Responsiveness of demand to a change in income: YED = %ΔQd ÷ %ΔY.
A normal good with YED > 1: demand rises more than proportionately as income rises.
A normal good with 0 < YED < 1: demand rises less than proportionately as income rises.
The shift of output and employment from primary to secondary and then tertiary sectors as incomes grow, linked to YED.
Responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price: PES = %ΔQs ÷ %ΔP.
Time period, spare capacity, ability to store stock, and mobility of factors of production.
A raw material or farm product (e.g. coffee, copper) whose demand and supply tend to be price inelastic, causing volatile prices.

questions.prompt: The price of a concert ticket rises from $40 to $50 and tickets sold fall from 2000 to 1800. What is PED?

questions.statement: If demand is price inelastic, a price rise increases total revenue.
questions.explanation: Quantity falls by a smaller percentage than price rises, so P × Q rises.

questions.text: When |PED| is greater than 1, demand is price ___.
questions.explanation: Quantity demanded is highly responsive to price.

questions.prompt: Which good is likely to have the MOST price elastic demand?
questions.explanation: A single brand has many close substitutes; the others are necessities with few substitutes or a small budget share.

questions.prompt: Match each PED value to its description.
questions.explanation: Economists usually compare the absolute value of PED with 1.

questions.prompt: A firm faces elastic demand and wants to raise total revenue. It should…
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, a price cut raises quantity by a larger percentage, so revenue rises.

questions.statement: Demand usually becomes more price elastic over a longer time period.
questions.explanation: Consumers have more time to find substitutes and change habits.

questions.prompt: Why does the government prefer to levy indirect taxes on goods with inelastic demand?
options: Consumers bear none of the tax
Quantity falls little, so tax revenue stays high
questions.explanation: Inelastic demand means a large tax base is maintained; but it does little to cut consumption.

questions.text: Price falls by 10% and quantity demanded rises by 15%. PED = ___.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to work out whether a price cut raises revenue.
items: Compare |PED| with 1 to judge the revenue effect
questions.explanation: If |PED| > 1 a price cut raises revenue; if < 1 it lowers it.

lessons.title: Income elasticity and price elasticity of supply

questions.prompt: Average income rises by 5% and demand for foreign holidays rises by 12%. What is YED and what type of good is it?
questions.explanation: YED = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4. Positive and above 1, so income elastic.

questions.statement: A good with a negative YED is an inferior good.
questions.explanation: Demand falls as income rises.

questions.text: A normal good with YED between 0 and 1 is a ___.
questions.explanation: Demand rises with income, but less than proportionately.

questions.prompt: Why does the share of agriculture in output tend to fall as a country grows richer?
options: Food has low YED, while demand for services has higher YED
questions.explanation: As incomes rise, spending on income-elastic services grows faster than on food: sectoral change.

questions.prompt: The price of strawberries rises by 20% and quantity supplied rises by 5% in the same week. What is PES?
questions.explanation: PES = 5 ÷ 20 = 0.25: inelastic, because farmers cannot grow more quickly.

questions.prompt: Match each factor to its effect on PES.

pairs.right: Output can rise quickly: more elastic
No stocks to release: less elastic
Time to expand capacity: more elastic
Hard to hire extra workers: less elastic

questions.explanation: PES depends on how easily firms can raise output when price rises.

questions.statement: Supply of primary commodities tends to be price inelastic in the short run.
questions.explanation: Crops and mines take a long time to expand, so short-run supply responds little to price.

questions.prompt: Why are prices of commodities such as coffee so volatile?
options: Both demand and supply are price inelastic, so shifts cause large price changes
questions.explanation: With steep curves, a small supply shock (e.g. drought) leads to a big price change.

questions.text: Manufactured goods tend to have ___ elastic supply than primary commodities.
questions.explanation: Factories can often increase shifts or use spare capacity quickly.

questions.prompt: Order these goods from lowest to highest likely YED.
questions.explanation: YED runs from negative for inferior goods to above 1 for luxuries.
